headline: Instinct is inherited wisdom—behaviors we're born knowing, without being taught
universal_truth: Some knowledge is ancient and reliable; some is outdated for modern conditions; wisdom is knowing which is which
fun_facts: Babies are born with a fear of falling and loud noises—no learning required
Sea turtles hatch on beaches and immediately head toward the ocean—they've never seen it before
The instinct to see faces is so strong that we see them in clouds, outlets, and car fronts—pareidolia
discussion_questions: What gut feelings do you trust?
When has instinct led you right or wrong?
How do you balance instinct and reason?

hook.script: No one taught you to be startled by sudden noises. No one taught you to prefer sweet over bitter. Some knowledge is installed at birth—ancient wisdom accumulated over millions of years, encoded in your biology. This is instinct.

cliff.script: Instincts evolved for ancestral environments. But we live in modern conditions. Can we trust what we're born knowing, or is instinct obsolete?
cliff.prompt: How should we relate to instinct?

options.text: Instinct is valuable data but not always accurate guidance—it evolved for different conditions, so verify before following blindly
options.response: Yes. Instinct is accumulated ancestral wisdom—worth listening to, but filtering through modern understanding. Fear of snakes: still useful. Fear of flying: mismatched to actual risk.

options.text: Trust your gut—it knows things your mind doesn't
options.response: Gut feelings capture real patterns, but they can also be outdated or miscalibrated...

fact1.title: Ancestral Wisdom
fact1.script: Instincts solved recurring problems our ancestors faced. Fear of heights prevented fatal falls. Disgust at rotten food prevented poisoning. These automatic responses kept us alive—no thinking required.

fact2.title: Mismatch Problems
fact2.script: Our instincts evolved for small tribes, scarce calories, and physical dangers. We now live in cities, abundant food, and abstract threats. Instincts for that world can misfire in this one—craving sugar, fearing strangers, seeking status.

fact3.title: Instinct Plus Reason
fact3.script: The best approach: listen to instinct as data, then process through reason. Gut feelings often detect patterns before conscious awareness. But instinct also creates biases. Use both systems together.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Some knowledge is ancient and reliable; some is outdated for modern conditions. Wisdom is knowing which is which—listen to instinct, but verify.

outro.script: That's Day 216. Tomorrow, we'll explore how your brain changes—neuroplasticity. Until then, notice an instinct and ask if it fits modern conditions.

growTrack.title: Instinct Check - Ancestral or Current?
growTrack.activity: Identify a strong gut feeling you have—about risk, people, situations. Ask: is this instinct calibrated for current reality, or for ancestral conditions? Use instinct as input, not final answer. Reason can update what instinct can't.
